description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the loss ratio (in percentage) and the number of TFLOPs (tera-floating-point operations) for four different models: Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The x-axis represents the TFLOPs on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, with tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 3e8, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, and 9e8. The y-axis represents the loss ratio in percentage, with a linear scale ranging from 94% to 100%, with major gridlines and labels at 94%, 95%, 96%, 97%, 98%, 99%, and 100%. The Vanilla model is represented by a purple line with triangle markers, which remains relatively flat at approximately 100% across the entire range of TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64) model is shown with an orange line and square markers, starting at around 98.1% and increasing to a peak of approximately 100.3% at 4e8 TFLOPs before slightly declining. The SepLLM (n=128) model is depicted with a blue line and cross markers, beginning at about 97.1% and steadily increasing to a peak of around 99.8% at 2e8 TFLOPs, then slightly decreasing. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model is represented by a green line with diamond markers, starting at approximately 97.5% and rising to a peak of about 100.2% at 5e8 TFLOPs, followed by a slight decline. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model is shown with a red line and circle markers, starting at 94% and increasing sharply to about 98.8% at 2e8 TFLOPs, then continuing to rise to a peak of approximately 99.1% at 4e8 TFLOPs before slightly declining.
